draft.title: Sketching a line from its intercepts
card: The y-intercept is where a line crosses the y-axis, where \(x = 0\). Put \(x = 0\) into the equation and solve for \(y\).
The x-intercept is where a line crosses the x-axis, where \(y = 0\). Put \(y = 0\) into the equation and solve for \(x\).
Plot \((0, 4)\) and \((6, 0)\). Then draw a straight line through them with a ruler.

4.alt: The line \(2x + 3y = 12\) through the y-intercept \((0, 4)\) and the x-intercept \((6, 0)\), going down to the right.

draft.remember: Two points fix a line: one with x equal to 0, one with y equal to 0.

a.q: What are the intercepts of the line \(3x - 2y = 12\)?
a.why: With \(x = 0\), \(-2y = 12\), so \(y = -6\). With \(y = 0\), \(3x = 12\), so \(x = 4\). The option \((0, 6)\) and \((4, 0)\) drops the negative sign when dividing by \(-2\).
a.clue: Solve one equation with x as 0, then one with y as 0.

b.q: Mei sketches \(y = 3x + 6\) by finding its intercepts. Which two points should she join?
b.why: With \(x = 0\), \(y = 6\). With \(y = 0\), \(3x = -6\), so \(x = -2\). The point \((2, 0)\) comes from losing the negative sign when moving the 6 across.
b.clue: Check the sign when you solve \(3x + 6 = 0\).
